title: WolfSociety: Understanding Collective Risk from Harmful-Agent Scaling in Financial Agent Societies
abstract: arXiv:2609.05591v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Safety evaluations typically focus on individual agents, but interacting agents can spread harmful information and influence the environment in which later decisions are made. We study how collective failure changes with harmful-agent fraction and society size in a controlled financial agent society, where agents communicate over a social network and trade in a shared market. In the primary financial scenario, collective failure requires broad harmful diffusion together with severe price dislocation or liquidity stress. Across all tested society sizes, failure remains rare at low harmful fractions but rises sharply over a narrow range. As society size grows from N=100 to N=2000, the harmful fraction associated with a 50% failure probability decreases from 4.7% to 2.2%, while the corresponding number of harmful agents increases from approximately 5 to 44. translated_title: WolfSociety：理解金融智能体社会中有害智能体规模化带来的集体风险
translated_abstract: 安全评估通常聚焦于单个智能体，但相互作用的智能体会传播有害信息，并影响后续决策所处的环境。我们在一个受控的金融智能体社会中研究集体失效如何随有害智能体比例和社会规模的变化而改变，在该社会中，智能体通过社交网络交流，并在共享市场中进行交易。在主要的金融场景中，集体失效需要有害信息的广泛扩散，同时伴随严重的价格错位或流动性压力。在所有测试的社会规模下，当有害比例较低时，失效仍然罕见，但在一个狭窄的区间内急剧上升。随着社会规模从 N=100 增长到 N=2000，对应 50% 失效概率的有害智能体比例从 4.7% 降至 2.2%，而相应的有害智能体数量则从约 5 个增加到 44 个。相比之下，当有害智能体的数量保持固定时，其影响变得……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过受控的金融智能体社会实验，首次揭示了集体失效风险的规模化规律：社会规模越大，引发50%失效所需的有害智能体比例越低（从4.7%降至2.2%），但有害智能体的绝对数量却随之增加。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a controlled financial agent society experiment revealing a scaling law of collective failure risk: as society size grows from 100 to 2000 agents, the harmful-agent fraction needed for 50% failure drops from 4.7% to 2.2%, while the absolute number of harmful agents increases from about 5 to 44.
